elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: The revised Section 14.4.2 still requires PB (Customer) to pay a liquidated sum on termination — "the sole amount payable by PB upon a given termination in Section 14.2, whether as liquidated damages or consideration for the Trial Data Package, shall be an early-termination fee not exceeding Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ during the three months preceding such termination". A capped fee is still a Customer-payable liquidated amount, so the preferred no-LD outcome is not reached; the 14.2.1/14.2.2/14.2.10 formulas (300%; Development Costs plus 25% p.a.) also remain in the text.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The proviso expressly recharacterises and confines the termination consideration: "the sole amount payable by PB upon a given termination in Section 14.2, whether as liquidated damages or consideration for the Trial Data Package, shall be an early-termination fee ...". The alternative-characterisation phrase closes the purchase-consideration route in 14.2/11.1.1.4, so the only liquidated amount PB can owe on termination is the early-termination fee. Retained Approval Payments under 14.2.2/14.2.10 are contingent post-approval milestone consideration, not liquidated damages, and Section 6.7 Buy-Out Payments are an elective prepayment, so neither displaces this element.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The fee is expressly capped: "an early-termination fee not exceeding Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ during the three months preceding such termination". The Agreement contains no periodic fee payable by PB pre-approval (Approval Payments are approval-contingent and the SFJ Interim Management Fee is a redacted lump sum), so Development Costs is the ascertainable running-spend analogue; the temporal anchor is exactly three months and is not exceeded.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: "[T]he sole amount payable by PB upon a given termination in Section 14.2, whether as liquidated damages or consideration for the Trial Data Package, shall be an early-termination fee ... in lieu of any claim for damages that SFJ may have", and the sentence opens "Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary", which reaches the Section 14.2 formulas (300%, 150%, Development Costs plus 25%). No other liquidated or penalty mechanic payable by PB survives (Section 6.4 default interest is compensatory interest, Section 6.7 Buy-Out Payments are elective).

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single edit to the Section 14.4.2 proviso converts every Section 14.2 termination payment into one early-termination fee, caps it at three months of Development Costs, and declares it the sole amount payable by PB whether framed as liquidated damages or as Trial Data Package consideration.

Preferred level is not reached and should not be claimed: a capped Customer-payable liquidated sum remains, and the 14.2.1/14.2.2/14.2.5.2/14.2.6/14.2.7/14.2.8.1/14.2.10 formulas are left in the text. Reaching preferred would require deleting each formula, which the rationale correctly identifies as a larger economic rewrite.

Minimal: one surgical replacement inside the existing proviso; the favourable retained language ("without prejudice to other remedies such Party may have at law or equity" and the "in lieu of any claim for damages that SFJ may have" tail) is preserved, no survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra damages category is added, and the pre-existing "Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary" opener is reused rather than a new override being bolted on. The added phrase "whether as liquidated damages or consideration for the Trial Data Package" is necessary, not surplus, because the Section 14.2 sums are framed as purchase consideration and would otherwise escape the cap.

Intent preserved: the Section 11.1.1.4 Trial Data Package purchase mechanic, the 14.2.2/14.2.10 credits for "the amount previously paid ... pursuant to this Section", the Section 6.2 adjustment, Section 6.7 Buy-Out Payments and post-approval Approval Payments all continue to operate against the capped fee; no defined term is orphaned and no cross-reference dangles.

Residual drafting risk to tighten (not a level failure): the retained 14.2 sentences still read "PB will pay SFJ ... an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs". The cap depends on the opening "Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary" carrying through the proviso. If SFJ pushes back, add "Notwithstanding Sections 14.2.1 through 14.2.10" inside the proviso itself (or conform each formula) so the override is beyond argument.

Second point to watch: the cap base is SFJ's spend rather than fees paid by PB. Confirm the three-month Development Costs figure is verifiable (e.g., tie it to the invoiced/reported Development Costs for the three calendar months preceding the termination effective date) so the ceiling cannot be inflated by costs merely "incurred" but unbilled.
